description: The desktop AI apps that make up the bulk of the demo table.
why: The four bundle ids that used to be must_contain are now must_find on the classifier, which is the layer that actually knows them. ChatGPT's id is a LIST because run 33511815638 showed the same cask resolving to two builds -- 26.721.41059 with com.openai.codex on macos-15, 1.2026.160 with com.openai.chat on macos-14 -- and both are real. It stays a raw probe rather than being dropped for the classifier: `chatgpt` matches on the brew route too, so must_find would still pass with every bundle id in the catalog broken, and this is the only assertion that reads the row. perplexity-desktop moved to 11-perplexity-desktop for its macOS >= 15 floor and is FORBIDDEN here rather than dropped: an assertion that merely stopped naming it could not tell 'no longer installed' from 'route quietly broken'.
known_gaps: Windsurf's Homebrew token is `devin-desktop`, not `windsurf`. Read off the Homebrew API; a scenario written from the product name would install nothing and the WARN would scroll past.
These are paid or account-gated products in several cases. The install is unattended and the SIGN-IN is not, so nothing here exercises behaviour that only appears once a user is authenticated.
The seventh cask, `perplexity`, is not installed here. It declares depends_on macos >= 15 and lives in 11-perplexity-desktop; splitting it out is what lets these six be tested on macos-14.

The macos-14 runner's Homebrew metadata is old enough to install a pre-rename ChatGPT. That is a fact about the runner, not about the product, and it will stop being true when the image updates -- at which point com.openai.chat survives only as the retired alias it is now recorded as, covered by a fixture rather than by this scenario.
